title: J&K Hands Salamabad Cross-LoC Trade Post to Tourism Department, Formally Ending 2008 Uri-Muzaffarabad Trade Route
detail: Under a September 12, 2026 order, the Jammu & Kashmir government formally handed over the Trade Facilitation Centre at Salamabad, Uri — one of two official cross-LoC trade points, opened in October 2008 to run a barter-trade route between Kashmir and Pakistan-administered Muzaffarabad — to the Tourism Department, which is repurposing the site for border tourism (accommodation rooms, a cafeteria, a park and LoC viewpoints in North Kashmir's Uri sector). Cross-LoC trade at Salamabad and the other crossing point, Chakan da Bagh in Poonch, had already been suspended indefinitely since April 2019, when India's Ministry of Home Affairs cited misuse of the routes for smuggling weapons, narcotics and fake currency, with several trading firms allegedly linked to banned militant organisations; the September conversion order closes the chapter formally rather than changing the on-the-ground trade freeze. PDP president Mehbooba Mufti objected publicly on September 20, urging Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to take the matter up with the Government of India and restore the centre's original purpose: 'The Salamabad Trade Facilitation Centre was built to bridge divided families, revive trade and heal wounds, not be reduced to a mere tourist site. It came at a heavy price, with many PDP workers losing their lives during the Muzaffarabad Chalo rally... Kashmir needs more bridges to the outside world, not the shutting of those that connect us.'

media.caption: The Salamabad Trade Facilitation Centre near Uri, handed over to J&K's Tourism Department, September 2026

confidenceReason: The handover order and its repurposing are reported consistently across multiple Kashmir-based outlets (ETV Bharat, Greater Kashmir, Kashmir Observer, Daily Excelsior, Kashmir Life) with a matching direct quote from PDP president Mehbooba Mufti; the underlying 2019 trade suspension is long-established fact.

title: Operation Sohan: Five J&K Districts Placed on High Alert as Injured JeM Militant Remains at Large
detail: Days after Army, J&K Police and CRPF killed two Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorists (identified as Saddam and Mustafa) in the Brattal Sohan/Khubban forest encounter near Udhampur's Majalta tehsil on the night of September 16-17, security agencies placed five J&K districts — Kathua, Samba, Udhampur, Doda and Kishtwar — on high alert, reported September 20, over concern that a third militant, believed injured in the initial exchange of fire, escaped into the forest and remains at large. Forces expanded the search beyond the original encounter site using drones, sniffer dogs and helicopters fitted with thermal surveillance to cover the difficult, densely forested terrain. Mobile phones and other equipment recovered from the two slain terrorists were sent for forensic examination to establish possible local support networks, and forensic teams examined blood traces along the injured militant's suspected escape route. No further casualties were reported as of September 20.
